stories.text: Woodthorpe House, of about 1750, is the oldest building in Sherwood.[^walk] It is now Sherwood Community Centre, at the north end of Mansfield Road opposite Woodthorpe Grange Park.

walk.title: Carrington and Sherwood walk (Nottingham Local Access Forum, 2018)

232140.sum: Woodthorpe House, on Mansfield Road. Today it houses Sherwood Community Centre. The building dates from the 19th century, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed.

credit.file: Sherwood Bus Depot at Melrose Street - Mansfield Road junction - geograph.org.uk - 6455898.jpg
credit.author: Luke Shaw

stories.text: Nottingham Corporation Tramways built the depot in 1900 when it carried the Carrington tram line on up Mansfield Road to Winchester Street. Trams ran until 6 September 1936, when buses replaced them. Part of the building is now the Samuel Hall pub, named after the man who laid out Sherwood.
Henry Ashwell, a Basford bleacher, built Woodthorpe Grange in 1874. The council bought the house and grounds in 1921 for £15,000, Jesse Boot giving £5,000 of it, and the park opened in 1922.
